decisions.candidate: APARELHO RESPIRATÓRIO (LARINGE/FARINGE) > Rinolalia; NARIZ E SEIOS PARANASAIS > Rinolalia
decisions.reason: Each utterance reports, in the first person, a voice or speech that sounds nasal (“anasalado”, “som nasal”, “ressonância nasal”, “sair pelo nariz”). Both printed descriptions say exactly that.

The entry is printed as “qualquer alteração da voz, como tom, volume ou qualidade”. A voice that has come to sound nasal is an alteration of how the voice sounds. The source treats the entry as an umbrella (Rouquidão is “um tipo de alteração da voz”), and the bank already keys Disfonia for Rinolalia, Rouquidão and Afonia stories. Stricter clinical usage separates resonance from phonation (B020-01).

decisions.reason: No utterance mentions a blocked or runny nose or difficulty breathing. Index 41 (“o som fica preso no nariz”) describes the sound.

decisions.candidate: LARINGE/FARINGE > Rouquidão / Afonia; APARELHO ENDOCRINOLÓGICO > Rouquidão
decisions.reason: No voice is described as rough or hoarse and none is lost; index 45 states “consigo falar”.
No difficulty articulating words, no change of rhythm and no language difficulty is described; the complaint is the sound of the voice.
Each utterance places the pain inside the throat (“garganta dolorida”, “dor por dentro da garganta”, “no fundo da garganta”).
Indices 51, 54 and 57 state that it hurts when swallowing water, food or saliva, with passage preserved.
Indices 50 and 56 report pain without eating or swallowing; indices 52, 53, 55, 58 and 59 do not mention swallowing. Silence is unknown, not evidence of pain on swallowing.
Indices 51, 54 and 57 deny difficulty in passage; the others do not mention swallowing. No burning sensation is described.

findings.issue: Indices 40–49 give full credit to three answers: Rinolalia in its two printed placements and Disfonia. The Disfonia path rests on the source's umbrella wording (“qualquer alteração da voz, como tom, volume ou qualidade”). The reviewer accepts it because the source itself is that broad: it describes Rinolalia as a “voz” with nasal resonance in the same group and calls Rouquidão “um tipo de alteração da voz”; and the bank already applies the same convention (the ten base-inventory Rinolalia stories key Rinolalia ×2 + Disfonia, the ten base Rouquidão stories key Disfonia, and indices 20–29 of this batch key Afonia + Disfonia). It is still a key-design choice. In stricter clinical usage a nasal voice is a resonance problem rather than a phonation problem, the expected term for “falo anasalado” is Rinolalia, and a teacher may prefer Disfonia not to be scored here. Indices 42 and 46 even rule out volume, leaving only “qualidade”.

findings.resolution: Passed. In the three utterances both facts are literal and independent: the pain is in the throat, and it comes on swallowing (water, lunch, saliva), with passage stated as preserved. In the seven Dor-only utterances the pain is either reported as present without eating or swallowing (50, 56) or swallowing is not mentioned (52, 53, 55, 58, 59), so Odinofagia is not supported. A teacher may want to confirm that throat pain felt only on swallowing should score under both entries.

findings.issue: The inventory has eight entries labelled “Dor” (this one plus 7 others: nose/sinuses, cardiovascular, skin, endocrine, hemolymphopoietic, male genital, breasts), as well as Nódulos (“caroço ou massa que sente ao apalpar”), Disfagia (“dificuldade para engolir.”) and Pirose. The ones that could be confused with throat pain are cardiovascular Dor (“pressão, dor ou desconforto no peito”), endocrine Dor (tenderness to touch in the anterior neck), hemolymphopoietic Dor (“dor ao apalpar pescoço”) and skin Dor.

findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with the key. All ten utterances place the pain inside the throat. Index 56 denies the chest; indices 52 and 59 deny skin pain, pain on touching and a tender lump; indices 51, 54 and 57 deny difficulty in passage (Disfagia). No utterance mentions burning. The inventory has no entry for throat clearing or a scratchy throat that could compete with index 53. Index 59 (“mais embaixo por dentro”) stays in the throat by the speaker's own words.

findings.issue: Index 41: “o som fica preso no nariz” may make a student think of a blocked nose. Indices 42 and 46: the nasal sound is reported only from a recording, and recorded voices often sound odd to the speaker. Index 47: the nasal sound is named by a colleague; the speaker only says they now pay attention to “esse som”. Index 54: the rationale stored on the Dor evidence entry is the story-level rationale and speaks about Odinofagia (“sustenta também Odinofagia”); the same reuse of the story rationale on the first evidence entry occurs in all twenty stories.
findings.resolution: None of these changes the term or opens another one, so the stories pass. Suggested polish for a later edit: 41 drop “preso”; 42 and 46 add that the sound is also heard in live conversation (as the base stories do); 47 add an explicit first-person confirmation; 54 give the Dor evidence its own rationale. No leftover naming a wrong symptom or term was found in any rationale.

Ressonância nasal da voz: Rinolalia nas duas entradas; mudança da voz: Disfonia pela descrição ampla (B020-01). “Não só em uma palavra” afasta a leitura de erro de pronúncia pontual.
